titulo: Why Do You Look Worse in Photos?
descripcion:
There are two versions of your face. One you've seen every day of your life. The other is the one everybody else sees.

The mirror flips you left to right, and you've spent your whole life memorising that reversed face. A photograph shows the un-flipped one - the version your friends fell for. Then add lens distortion, a frozen frame and a smile you performed on command.

In this video:
00:00 Two versions of your face
00:35 The mirror is backwards
01:35 The 1977 study that settles it
03:00 Nobody's face is symmetrical
04:29 The lens is lying too
05:26 The frozen frame problem
06:53 The camera changes your face
07:46 So which one is real?

Sources: Mita, Dermer & Knight 1977 on mirror-image preference; Zajonc on the mere-exposure effect; Ward et al. 2018, JAMA Facial Plastic Surgery, on selfie distance and nasal distortion; Post et al. 2012 on the frozen face effect.

New video every day.
